text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Streaming tail latency p99 > 5s for /v1/stream (us-east-2). SLO breach threshold crossed. Notifying on-call. ticket: INC-2026-1593

sara: ack oncall here — seeing alerts. paging infra + netops. any customer escalations yet?

mike: seeing p95 around 800ms -> p99 jumped to 5.2s since 02:10 UTC. throughput steady. attaching grafana snapshot (query: sum by(route){latency_p95,latency_p99}). link: https://grafana.internal/streams/alert/187650

ana: quick check of host-level metrics — TCP retransmit rate spiked on proxy fleet in az-c. pod restarts? no. netdev rx_errs rising on a subset of ENIs in az-c -> possible cross-AZ path issue.

jess: customers reporting streaming stalls and reconnects. I saw 3 support tickets citing partial response bodies and then long delays. All from eu-west customers routed via us-east2 for model shards.

kevin: running quick tcpdump on a sample pod in az-c, saw repeated SYN retries and TLS renegotiation attempts. TLS handshake time series shows spikes to 3-4s. Could be packet loss or ECMP path causing reordering.

ana: pulled VPC Flow logs for the ENIs with rx_errs — a bunch of TCP retransmits to NAT gateway IPs and ICMP frag-needed messages. looks like MTU path issue between az-c and a peered network hop.

sara: MTU... interesting. Did we roll any network policy or change recently?

mike: there was a kpatch on our egress NAT autoscaler earlier but logs show normal. cloud provider deployed a routing flap in az-c at 01:58 UTC (provider event id: cloud-rt-1129). They claim transient, but metrics started at 02:06 UTC.

jess: impact table: streaming endpoints p95 -> +600ms, p99 -> +3-5s, tail stalls causing partial client reconnects. high-impact for long-response streaming customers (realtime transcripts). Potentially severe for SLAs.

kevin: mitigation plan attempt 1: fail traffic away from az-c by adjusting our smart-routing policy to prefer az-a/az-b for new streaming sessions. Doing a canary reroute for 10% now.

devops-bot: traffic-shift job started: route-adjust --service streams --from az-c --weight -10% --to az-a,az-b --canary=10

ana: after canary shift p99 in canary traffic down to ~900ms. az-c still noisy for sessions pinned earlier because of existing TCP connections.

sara: good. we need two more mitigation tracks: 1) work with cloud provider to fix MTU/path or provide a temporary alternate egress, 2) provide graceful reconnect for pinned sessions (shorter keepalive + client backoff).

mike: opening a support case with provider, pushing VPC trace and ICMP frag-needed logs. case: CP-67821. provider suggests increasing PMTU discovery timeouts; dubious as fix.

jess: prod code change: reduce our streaming session keepalive to 10s and aggressive reconnect jitter for new clients. can ship a config flip to edge proxies in 2-3 min. should unstick some pinned sessions.

kevin: rolling config change to edge-proxy (canary to 20%): kubectl set env deploy/edge-proxy KEEPALIVE=10 RECONNECT_JITTER=0.2 -n prod

ana: also adding iptables rule on affected hosts to drop ICMP frag-needed toward NAT IP to force path MTU fallback? risky. I'd rather avoid if provider can patch.

sara: don't modify iptables broadly. coordinate with kevin and provider first. prioritized: 1) traffic shift, 2) proxy keepalive flip, 3) provider escalations.

devops-bot: deploy edge-proxy env change completed for 20% canary at 02:36 UTC.

mike: monitoring — canary p99 is 820ms, overall p99 climbed down to 2.1s (was 5.2s). impressions: routing change removed new sessions from bad path but long-lived streams still hit tail latency.

jess: sending one-liner to CX: "We're investigating streaming stalls in us-east-2. Some customers may experience intermittent delays; we're routing new sessions away from affected AZ and applying mitigations. We'll update within 30 minutes."

sara: customer comms sent. escalation: DRI on-call remains sara, handoff to kevin at 03:30 UTC if not resolved.

ana: provider response: routed engineer onsite to the routing fabric, found an MTU mismatch on a peering hop causing fragment-needed messages. provider applying fix to restore path MTU. ETA 18-25 minutes.

kevin: standing by to scale NAT gateway pool if provider fix delayed. Could also spin up ephemeral NAT in az-a and az-b and route traffic. Doing a dry-run for nat-provision script.

mike: dry-run succeeded. provisioning ephemeral egress in az-a now as precaution.

devops-bot: ephemeral-nat provision job start --zone az-a --size small --tag incident-187650

jess: CX asked for updated ETA. I told them ~20 mins and that we've routed new sessions away.

ana: provider reports fix rolled at 02:58 UTC. we're seeing fewer ICMP frag-needed events and retransmit rate dropping on affected ENIs.

mike: metrics now: p95 280ms, p99 680ms, retransmit rate back to baseline. streaming tail errors down 92% vs peak.

sara: great. keep monitoring for 1h. kevin you can cancel nat provisioning if not needed.

kevin: canceling ephemeral-nat job. leaving routing policy in prefer-az for 30m to allow pinned sessions to drain.

jess: CX updated: issue mitigated; provider applied fix; we routed traffic and applied proxy reconnect policy; monitoring for residual impact.

sara: creating post-incident doc: INC-2026-1593 root cause initial: provider peering hop MTU mismatch causing packet fragmentation and TLS handshake retries -> increased tail latency for streaming. action items: 1) automate early ICMP/MTU alerts, 2) add fallback egress provisioning playbook, 3) revisit session pinning strategy for cross-AZ resilience. assigning owners.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (monitoring): severity: high -> resolved at 03:20 UTC. ticket: INC-2026-1593.

sara: thanks all. handoff reminder: kevin will take on-call at 03:30 UTC. leave notes in the incident doc and I'll start RCA draft. :thumbsup:
